title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 95
paragraphs: When these newly appointed commanders, marching from the king, reached the Aleïan plain in Cilicia at the head of a large and well-equipped land army, the whole naval armament also arrived, drawn from the several nations that had been assigned to provide it. There too came the horse-transports that Darius the year before had ordered his tributaries to have ready. Into these they embarked their cavalry, and having loaded the land-army on the ships, they set sail for Ionia with six hundred triremes. Instead of keeping their course along the mainland towards the Hellespont and Thrace, they set out from Samos and made their voyage through the Icarian Sea, between the islands — because, I think, they feared above all the coastline around Mount Athos, since the previous year, going that way, they had suffered a terrible disaster. Besides, Naxos was forcing their hand, since it had not been subdued the first time.
